intro: Hi, and welcome to your first English lesson! Today you learn how to say hello and goodbye at any time of day, the magic words please, thank you, sorry and excuse me, and how to answer How are you?. Warm-up: how do you say 'selamat pagi' in English?
teachingNotes: This is the learner's very first lesson: teach whole phrases as fixed chunks (I'm fine, you're welcome, see you). Do not explain the verb 'to be', tenses or any other grammar yet.

Indonesian times of day don't map one to one: siang and sore are both 'Good afternoon' (12 noon to about 6 p.m.), and 11 a.m. is still 'Good morning'. 'Selamat malam' is 'Good evening' when you arrive but 'Good night' when you leave or go to bed. The most common error is saying 'Good night' when arriving in the evening. There is no 'Good noon'.

Indonesian 'maaf' covers two English words: 'sorry' after a mistake, and 'excuse me' before a question, to call someone or to pass (Indonesian 'permisi'). 'Sama-sama' is 'You're welcome', never 'same-same'.

'How are you?' is part of hello: the answer is short and positive, with thanks and a question back (I'm fine, thanks. And you?). Learners sometimes confuse it with 'Who are you?' and answer with their name.
Show register simply: Hi / Bye / Thanks with friends; Good morning / Goodbye / Thank you with teachers, bosses and customers. Add please to requests, because a bare request can sound rude in English.
Prompts use a.m. and p.m., which many Indonesian learners don't use: a.m. = from midnight to 12 noon (pagi), p.m. = from 12 noon to midnight (siang, sore, malam). Explain it if the learner hesitates.

Learners meet short forms here: I'm = I am, you're = you are. Just say they are the short forms people use when speaking and that I'm fine / You're welcome are learnt as whole phrases. Don't teach 'to be' yet.

Warn against word-by-word translation of fixed phrases: How are you? = apa kabar? (not 'bagaimana kamu'), See you = sampai jumpa (not 'lihat kamu'), You're welcome = sama-sama, and Not bad = lumayan, which is a positive answer even though it contains 'bad'.
'Mum' in the examples is British; Americans write and say 'Mom'. Both mean ibu.

keyPoints.title: Hello and goodbye at any time of day
keyPoints.explanation: Hello and Hi work at any time. Good morning (until 12 noon), Good afternoon (12 noon to about 6 p.m.), Good evening (after about 6 p.m., when you arrive). To leave: Goodbye, Bye, See you. Good night only when you leave at night or go to bed.

id.title: Halo dan sampai jumpa di jam berapa pun
id.explanation: Hello dan Hi bisa dipakai kapan saja. Good morning (sampai jam 12 siang), Good afternoon (jam 12 siang sampai sekitar jam 6 sore), Good evening (setelah sekitar jam 6 sore, saat kamu datang). Untuk pamit: Goodbye, Bye, See you. Good night hanya saat kamu pamit di malam hari atau mau tidur.

keyPoints.title: Please, thank you, sorry, excuse me
keyPoints.explanation: Please makes a request polite. Thank you (or Thanks) when someone helps you; the reply is You're welcome. Sorry comes after a mistake. Excuse me comes before you ask a stranger something, call someone or pass.

examples.en: Thank you very much! — You're welcome.
Excuse me, where is the toilet?

id.title: Please, thank you, sorry, excuse me
id.explanation: Please membuat permintaan jadi sopan. Thank you (atau Thanks) saat seseorang membantumu; jawabannya You're welcome. Sorry diucapkan setelah berbuat salah. Excuse me diucapkan sebelum kamu bertanya ke orang yang tidak dikenal, memanggil seseorang, atau mau lewat.

keyPoints.title: How are you?
keyPoints.explanation: How are you? is part of saying hello. Answer short, say thanks and ask back: I'm fine, thanks. And you? Other good answers: I'm good, Very well, Not bad. I'm is the short form of I am. Not bad sounds negative but means 'lumayan', a good answer.

id.title: How are you? (Apa kabar?)
id.explanation: How are you? adalah bagian dari menyapa. Jawab singkat, ucapkan terima kasih, lalu tanya balik: I'm fine, thanks. And you? Jawaban bagus lainnya: I'm good, Very well, Not bad. I'm adalah bentuk pendek dari I am. Not bad terdengar negatif, tapi artinya 'lumayan', jawaban yang baik.

guidedPractice.prompt: It's 7 a.m. You meet your neighbour Pak Joko. Complete: Good ___, Pak Joko!
Your friend says 'Thank you!' Write a polite reply.
Order politely at a warung. Complete: Two nasi goreng, ___.
Answer the question short and polite: How are you?
guidedPractice.hint: Say how you feel, then thank the person.

independentPractice.prompt: It's 10 p.m. You go home from Rina's house. What do you say to her? (two words)
independentPractice.hint: You are leaving, and it's late.

independentPractice.prompt: You arrive late to class. Say sorry to the teacher.
Rina says: 'I'm fine, thanks. And you?' Answer her.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. It's 2 p.m. You walk into Bu Ani's office. Complete: Good ___, Bu Ani!
assessment.rubric: Correct: afternoon (12 noon to about 6 p.m.). 'morning', 'evening', 'night' or 'noon' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. It's Tuesday afternoon. You leave the office. Your next meeting with your colleague is on Wednesday morning. Complete: See you ___!
assessment.rubric: Correct: tomorrow. Also accept '(on) Wednesday'. 'later' = 60 (true but not the best answer). 'Good night' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Choose the correct answer. A shop assistant at Indomaret gives you your change. What do you say to her?
assessment.rubric: Correct: Thank you / Thanks (any polite thanks). 'Sorry', 'Please' or 'You're welcome' = 0.

assessment.prompt: You are lost in Bandung and want to ask a stranger a question. What two words do you say first?
assessment.rubric: Correct: Excuse me. 'Sorry' = 50 (possible, but excuse me is the best way to start). 'Please' or 'Hello' = 30.

assessment.prompt: It's 8 a.m. You meet Dimas. Choose the greeting for this time.
assessment.rubric: Needs a greeting (Hi / Hello / Good morning) and 'How are you?'. Missing the greeting = 60. 'Who are you?' = 0 for the question part. 'Good evening/night' = 50.

assessment.prompt: Listen to the greeting. Choose a polite reply.
assessment.rubric: Needs a short positive answer (I'm fine / good / very well / not bad) and a question back (And you? / How about you?). Answer without the question back = 70. Giving a name ('I'm Rina') = 0.

material.title: Hello at any time of day

blocks.text: Say **Hello** at any time of day. **Hi** is relaxed, for friends and family. To be a bit more polite, use the time of day: **Good morning** (until 12 noon), **Good afternoon** (12 noon to about 6 p.m.) and **Good evening** (after about 6 p.m.).

id.text: Ucapkan **Hello** kapan saja. **Hi** lebih santai, untuk teman dan keluarga. Supaya lebih sopan, pakai salam sesuai waktu: **Good morning** (sampai jam 12 siang), **Good afternoon** (jam 12 siang sampai sekitar jam 6 sore) dan **Good evening** (setelah sekitar jam 6 sore).

rows.note: after about 6 p.m., when you arrive

id.note: setelah sekitar jam 6 sore, saat kamu datang

blocks.text: **a.m. and p.m.** English often writes the time with **a.m.** (from midnight to 12 noon: *pagi*) or **p.m.** (from 12 noon to midnight: *siang, sore, malam*). So *7 a.m.* is jam 7 pagi, *4 p.m.* is jam 4 sore and *8 p.m.* is jam 8 malam. Look for a.m. or p.m. first, then choose the greeting.

id.text: **a.m. dan p.m.** Bahasa Inggris sering menulis jam dengan **a.m.** (dari tengah malam sampai jam 12 siang: *pagi*) atau **p.m.** (dari jam 12 siang sampai tengah malam: *siang, sore, malam*). Jadi *7 a.m.* artinya jam 7 pagi, *4 p.m.* jam 4 sore, dan *8 p.m.* jam 8 malam. Lihat dulu a.m. atau p.m., baru pilih salamnya.

blocks.text: Indonesian has four times of day (pagi, siang, sore, malam), but English greetings have three. **Selamat siang** and **selamat sore** are both **Good afternoon**, and at 11 a.m. it's still **Good morning**. There is no 'Good noon'.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia punya empat waktu (pagi, siang, sore, malam), tapi salam bahasa Inggris hanya tiga. **Selamat siang** dan **selamat sore** sama-sama **Good afternoon**, dan jam 11 pagi masih **Good morning**. Tidak ada 'Good noon'.

blocks.prompt: It's 11 a.m. You call a client in Jakarta. How do you start?
blocks.explain: Until 12 noon it's Good morning in English, even when Indonesians already say selamat siang.

id.explain: Sampai jam 12 siang, bahasa Inggris memakai Good morning, walaupun orang Indonesia sudah bilang selamat siang.
id.prompt: Jam 11 pagi. Kamu menelepon klien di Jakarta. Kamu mulai dengan apa?

blocks.text: When you leave, say **Goodbye** (polite) or **Bye** (relaxed). Add **See you!**, **See you later!** or **See you tomorrow!** When you leave at night or go to bed, say **Good night**. **See you** is a fixed phrase that means *sampai jumpa*: don't translate it word by word ('lihat kamu').

id.text: Saat pergi, ucapkan **Goodbye** (sopan) atau **Bye** (santai). Tambahkan **See you!**, **See you later!** atau **See you tomorrow!** Kalau kamu pulang malam hari atau mau tidur, ucapkan **Good night**. **See you** adalah ungkapan tetap yang artinya *sampai jumpa*: jangan diterjemahkan kata per kata ('lihat kamu').

rows.en: Goodbye, Pak Hasan. See you on Monday.
rows.id: Sampai jumpa, Pak Hasan. Sampai ketemu hari Senin.

rows.note: going to bed · Mum is British, Americans say Mom

id.note: mau tidur · Mum itu bahasa Inggris British, orang Amerika bilang Mom

blocks.text: **Good night** is only for leaving at night or going to bed. When you **arrive** in the evening, say **Good evening**. Indonesian *selamat malam* covers both, English doesn't.

id.text: **Good night** hanya untuk berpamitan di malam hari atau sebelum tidur. Saat kamu **datang** di malam hari, ucapkan **Good evening**. *Selamat malam* dipakai untuk keduanya, tapi bahasa Inggris membedakannya.

blocks.prompt: It's 9 p.m. Your guests are going home. What do you say?
blocks.explain: They are leaving at night, so Good night. Good evening is for when people arrive.

id.explain: Mereka pulang di malam hari, jadi Good night. Good evening dipakai saat orang datang.
id.prompt: Jam 9 malam. Tamumu mau pulang. Apa yang kamu ucapkan?

blocks.text: **Please** makes a request polite. Put it **at the end** when you ask for something (*Two teas, please.* = Minta dua teh) and **at the start** when you invite someone to do something (*Please come in.* = Silakan masuk). That's why one English *please* can be *minta*, *tolong* or *silakan* in Indonesian. Say **Thank you** (or **Thanks** with friends) when someone helps you or gives you something. The answer to *Thank you* is **You're welcome** or **No problem**.

id.text: **Please** membuat permintaan jadi sopan. Taruh **di akhir** saat kamu meminta sesuatu (*Two teas, please.* = Minta dua teh) dan **di awal** saat kamu mempersilakan orang melakukan sesuatu (*Please come in.* = Silakan masuk). Karena itu satu kata *please* bisa berarti *minta*, *tolong* atau *silakan*. Ucapkan **Thank you** (atau **Thanks** ke teman) saat seseorang membantumu atau memberimu sesuatu. Jawaban untuk *Thank you* adalah **You're welcome** atau **No problem**.

blocks.text: *Sama-sama* is **You're welcome**, not 'same-same'. Learn *You're welcome* as one fixed phrase: don't translate *welcome* here. (*You're* is the short form of *you are*.) And use please a lot: in English a request without it can sound rude.

id.text: *Sama-sama* adalah **You're welcome**, bukan 'same-same'. Hafalkan *You're welcome* sebagai satu ungkapan utuh: kata *welcome* di sini tidak perlu diterjemahkan. (*You're* adalah bentuk pendek dari *you are*.) Dan sering-seringlah memakai please: dalam bahasa Inggris, permintaan tanpa please bisa terdengar kasar.

blocks.explain: No problem (or You're welcome) answers thanks. 'Same-same' is a direct translation of sama-sama and isn't English.

id.explain: No problem (atau You're welcome) adalah jawaban untuk ucapan terima kasih. 'Same-same' terjemahan langsung dari sama-sama dan bukan bahasa Inggris.
id.prompt: Lengkapi jawabanmu. Budi: 'Thanks for your help!' Kamu: '___'

blocks.text: Indonesian *maaf* can be two English words. Say **Sorry** (or **I'm sorry**) **after** a small mistake: you're late, you bump into someone. Say **Excuse me** **before** you ask a stranger something, call a waiter or need to pass someone. Indonesian *permisi* is usually **Excuse me**.

id.text: *Maaf* dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa menjadi dua kata bahasa Inggris. Ucapkan **Sorry** (atau **I'm sorry**) **setelah** kesalahan kecil: kamu terlambat, kamu menabrak orang. Ucapkan **Excuse me** **sebelum** bertanya kepada orang asing, memanggil pelayan, atau saat mau lewat. *Permisi* biasanya **Excuse me**.

rows.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

rows.note: to pass someone on a busy KRL train

id.note: untuk lewat di KRL yang penuh

blocks.prompt: You bump into a woman at the market. What do you say?
blocks.explain: Bumping into someone is a small mistake, so say sorry.

id.explain: Menabrak orang adalah kesalahan kecil, jadi ucapkan sorry.
id.prompt: Kamu menabrak seorang ibu di pasar. Apa yang kamu ucapkan?

blocks.text: **How are you?** is part of saying hello. Give a short, positive answer, say thanks, and ask back: **I'm fine, thanks. And you?** Other good answers: **I'm good**, **Very well, thank you** (polite) and **Not bad**. Nobody wants a long story here!

id.text: **How are you?** adalah bagian dari menyapa. Jawab singkat dan positif, ucapkan terima kasih, lalu tanya balik: **I'm fine, thanks. And you?** Jawaban lain yang bagus: **I'm good**, **Very well, thank you** (sopan) dan **Not bad**. Di sini tidak perlu cerita panjang!

rows.en: Good morning, Pak Hasan. How are you?
rows.id: Selamat pagi, Pak Hasan. Apa kabar?

rows.en: Very well, thank you. And you?
rows.id: Baik sekali, terima kasih. Bapak sendiri?

rows.en: Not bad, thanks. How about you?

blocks.text: Don't mix up **How are you?** (apa kabar?) and **Who are you?** (kamu siapa?). Answer *How are you?* with how you feel, not with your name.

id.text: Jangan tertukar **How are you?** (apa kabar?) dan **Who are you?** (kamu siapa?). Jawab *How are you?* dengan keadaanmu, bukan dengan namamu.

blocks.text:
Three things that can look strange:
- **I'm** is the short form of **I am** (*saya*). People almost always say *I'm* when they speak.
- **How are you?** is one fixed question that means *apa kabar?*. Don't translate it word by word.
- **Not bad** has the word *bad* (*jelek*), but it means *lumayan, cukup baik*. It's a positive answer.

id.text:
Tiga hal yang mungkin terasa aneh:
- **I'm** adalah bentuk pendek dari **I am** (*saya*). Saat bicara, orang hampir selalu bilang *I'm*.
- **How are you?** adalah satu pertanyaan tetap yang artinya *apa kabar?*. Jangan diterjemahkan kata per kata.
- **Not bad** memang ada kata *bad* (*jelek*), tapi artinya *lumayan, cukup baik*. Itu jawaban yang positif.

blocks.prompt: Rina: 'How are you?' Which answer is best?
blocks.explain: How are you? asks how you feel: answer short, say thanks and ask back.

id.explain: How are you? menanyakan keadaanmu: jawab singkat, ucapkan terima kasih, lalu tanya balik.
id.prompt: Rina: 'How are you?' Jawaban mana yang paling tepat?
